summary.value: The Valdarnese is a big white meat chicken from the upper valley of the Arno river in Tuscany, between Florence and Arezzo. White chickens from this valley were first written about in 1899. The breed had a club by 1955, but it faded fast in the 1960s as old sharecropping farms broke up and cheap White Leghorn chicks took over, and by the end of the century it had nearly vanished. A rescue program began in the 1990s, and Tuscany now keeps a breed register and standard. Around 1,200 breeding birds were counted in 2007. The plumage is white, the skin yellow and the legs orange yellow, with a large red single comb. Roosters weigh about 6.4 to 7.3 pounds and hens about 4.4 to 5.5 pounds. Hens go broody often, so they lay only about 135 ivory eggs a year. Its firm meat is the main reason it is raised.
